title.en: Finding Your Human Voice in the Age of AI

narrative_brief: Mini PechaKucha for Science Communication (SDG 9 × AI Literacy × Science Communication)

A2.text: Good morning, everyone. Today we look at United Nations SDG 9. It is a global plan. It helps countries build better factories and support new science.

A2.workbook_text: Good morning, everyone. Today, let’s look at United Nations SDG 9, which is a great global plan that helps all countries build better factories, support new science projects, and make modern technology for a much better world.

B1.text: Good morning, everyone. Today, let’s look at United Nations SDG 9, a global goal that encourages all countries to support modern technology and build strong networks for a better world.

B2.text: Good morning, everyone. Today, let’s explore United Nations SDG 9, a global framework that encourages countries to upgrade industry, support modern innovation, and build resilient infrastructure for sustainable scientific development worldwide.

A2.text: AI is changing science very fast. It also changes how we share ideas. But the quality of the answer depends on one thing: how we ask.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: In our world today, Artificial Intelligence is changing scientific research and communication very quickly; however, the quality of the AI's answer always depends on one very important thing—how we talk to the computer.

B1.text: In our modern digital world, Artificial Intelligence is changing scientific research and communication very quickly; however, the quality of AI's answers depends on one important factor—how we talk to it.

B2.text: In this digital era, Artificial Intelligence is rapidly transforming scientific research, communication, and innovation; however, the actual quality of AI's output depends greatly on one critical factor—how we communicate with it.

stages.language_pattern: present progressive for trends / this causes ...

A2.text: Many science students use ChatGPT or Gemini. We fix lab reports with it. We read short summaries. We ask about hard homework. It is fast and easy.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: As university science students, many of us often use ChatGPT or Gemini to fix our weekly lab reports, read short summaries of long science articles, or explain difficult homework ideas because it is very fast and easy.

B1.text: As university science students, many of us often use ChatGPT to improve our lab reports, read short summaries of science articles, or explain difficult concepts during our weekly assignments.

B2.text: As university science majors, many of us frequently rely on ChatGPT to improve laboratory reports, summarize complex journal articles, or explain difficult scientific concepts during our weekly academic routines.

A2.text: This tool is convenient. But some students give too little information. Then the AI writes boring, repeated text. People call this AI slop. It has no real value.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: Although this new technology is very convenient, many lazy students want good answers without giving enough information, so the AI gives boring, repetitive, and useless responses that people call "AI slop" because it has no real value.

B1.text: Although this technology is fast, many students expect useful answers without giving enough information, which creates boring or unrelated responses commonly called "AI slop" that has no real value.

B2.text: Although this technology is fast and convenient, many students expect useful answers without providing enough information, resulting in vague, repetitive, or unrelated responses commonly known as "AI slop" that provides little real value.

A2.text: Why does this happen? The AI does not understand your ideas. It only guesses the next word. It uses the words in your prompt. Few details bring wrong answers.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: Why does this happen? The AI computer does not automatically understand your human ideas; instead, it only guesses the next word by looking at the small words in your prompt, so the answer becomes wrong when you give no details.

B1.text: Why does this happen? AI does not automatically understand what we want; instead, it only guesses the next word based on our prompt, making the answer wrong when context is missing.

B2.text: Why does this happen? AI does not automatically understand our human intentions; instead, it predicts responses strictly based on the information contained in our prompt, making the output less accurate when context is missing.

A2.text: A good prompt has four parts. Give a role. Give background facts. Give a clear goal. Give simple rules. Clear instructions bring much better answers.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: To fix this problem, a good prompt must always include a clear role, helpful background facts, simple goals, and clear rules, because giving very clear instructions always helps the AI give us much better and more useful answers.

B1.text: To fix this, a good prompt must include a clear role, helpful background facts, clear goals, and simple limits, because clearer instructions always give us more reliable AI answers.

B2.text: To fix this, a well-designed prompt must include a clear role, sufficient background information, specific goals, and realistic limitations, because clearer instructions always make the AI's response more relevant and reliable.

A2.text: Clear writing matters in science. Good prompts help our lab reports. They also help our presentations. Our work becomes faster and more correct.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: In scientific research, being clear and precise is very important for everyone, and learning to write great prompts can directly help our school lab reports and science presentations, making our university work much faster and more correct.

B1.text: In scientific research, precise communication is very important, and learning to write good prompts can directly improve our lab reports and science presentations, making our work much faster and more accurate.

B2.text: In scientific research, precise communication is absolutely essential, and learning to write well-constructed prompts can directly improve our literature reviews, laboratory reports, and scientific presentations, making our research both more efficient and more accurate.

A2.text: But do not copy the answer without thinking. You will stop learning. Real science starts with human curiosity. It does not start with fast answers.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: However, if students just copy and paste these computer answers without thinking, they will stop learning and become very lazy, forgetting that true science must always begin with active human curiosity and not just digital convenience.

B1.text: However, if students simply accept these computer answers without thinking, they might become passive learners, forgetting that true science always begins with active curiosity rather than digital convenience.

B2.text: However, if students simply accept these automated answers without questioning them, they risk becoming passive learners, forgetting that true scientific thinking must always begin with active curiosity rather than digital convenience.

title.zh: AI 素養策略一： 提問前的後設認知

A2.text: So think before you type. Ask yourself one question. What do I really need? Who will read this? Which format is best for this task?
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: Therefore, before you type a prompt, you must first think about your final goal by asking yourself what information you really need, who your audience is, and what kind of text format is best for your science task.

B1.text: Therefore, before writing a prompt, you must first think about your goal by asking yourself what information you really need, who your audience is, and what response is best for your task.

B2.text: Therefore, before writing a prompt, you must first identify your objective by asking yourself what information you truly need, who your target audience is, and what type of response would be most useful for your task.

title.zh: AI 素養策略二： 具體動作

A2.text: Then give the AI clear instructions. Add your student background. Add the format you want. Prompt writing is science communication too.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: Then, give the AI your clear and organized instructions, including your student background and your expected format, because we should see prompt writing as another very important way to talk about science like a professional.

B1.text: Then, provide the AI with organized instructions, including your academic background and expected format, because we should see prompt writing as another important form of professional scientific communication.

B2.text: Then, provide the AI with organized instructions, including your academic background and expected format, because we should see prompt writing as another important form of professional scientific communication.

stages.source_description: The Human Edge: Redefining the human role

title.en: The Human Edge: Redefining the human role

A2.text: Computers organize data very well. But they have no curiosity. They have no intuition. They have no honest heart. People turn numbers into new discoveries.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: In this high-tech world, computers can easily organize data, but they completely lack human scientific curiosity, natural intuition, and honest hearts, which are special human qualities that turn simple numbers into amazing new scientific discoveries.

B1.text: In this high-tech world, computers can easily organize data, but they completely lack human scientific curiosity, natural intuition, and honest hearts, which are irreplaceable qualities that turn facts into real discoveries.

B2.text: In this automated world, algorithms can easily organize data, but they completely lack human scientific curiosity, professional intuition, and ethical responsibility, which are irreplaceable qualities that turn raw data into meaningful discoveries.

source_notes.outline_section: 人類獨特價值： 用 high-tech world, natural intuition, honest hearts 做出完美、有溫度且好唸的對

title.en: Final Call to Action: The SDG 9 future vision

A2.text: In conclusion, good innovation starts with good communication. Better prompts bring better answers. But scientists still think carefully every day. Thank you.
A2.basis: Replaces the original A2 column of sheet 'SDG9-2 (A2)', which averaged 31.9 words per sentence (one long sentence per slide) and read at roughly B2. Meaning, slide order and every claim are unchanged; only the sentence structure is split. Spec: <=35 words per slide, <=12 words per sentence.
A2.workbook_text: In conclusion, good innovation under SDG 9 begins with good communication, because while better prompts bring better answers, smart scientists create useful knowledge by talking very clearly and thinking carefully every single day. Thank you.

B1.text: In conclusion, responsible innovation under SDG 9 begins with responsible communication, because while better prompts bring better answers, thoughtful scientists create meaningful knowledge by talking clearly and thinking critically.

B2.text: In conclusion, responsible innovation under SDG 9 begins with responsible communication, meaning that while better prompts produce better responses, thoughtful scientists create meaningful knowledge by communicating clearly and thinking critically.
